correctness.rationale: Currie–Ochem–Rampersad–Shallit prove rho_p(n)=2n+1. The generated prefix realizes exactly this many factors at each length 1 through 8, so those finite sets are exhaustive. The complete length-8 set has no word whose reversal is also present. Any reflected pair at a longer length would contain a reflected length-8 prefix/suffix pair, so none exists. The complete shorter sets give the stated reflection-class counts; at length 7 the only reversible factor is the palindrome 1012101, so no two distinct factors merge. The verifier regenerates all finite evidence from the defining morphism.

value.rationale: The 2024 paper identifies eventual reversal avoidance as directly relevant to reflection complexity but leaves many concrete sequences unanalyzed. This word is a canonical ternary low-factor-complexity example already singled out because its language is not reversal-closed. Determining the exact first reversal-free length is therefore a natural finite cutoff, and it completely determines a new complexity profile rather than supplying an arbitrary isolated table value.
